rows.description: A parent who shouted or was absent returns, names what happened and apologises without excuses. Repair teaches a teenager that relationships can survive mistakes, and it counts more than never erring.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A person who grew up with insecure bonds can become more secure through a steady friend, mentor, partner or therapist. Repeated experience of reliability, plus reflecting on past patterns, shifts expectations.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A wise person treats attachment styles as tendencies that vary with context, not as identity or excuse. Uses them to understand reactions, and still takes responsibility for behaviour.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 23–26

rows.subtype: Patterns triggered by a partner's style [Observer]
rows.description: An anxious person paired with an avoidant one often loops: pursuit and withdrawal feed each other. Seeing the loop as a shared pattern rather than one person's fault opens a way out.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A child feels valuable only when they score high or win praise, and crumbles after a poor result. Worth is conditional, so ordinary setbacks feel like proof of being not enough.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A parent or teacher praises effort, strategy and kindness rather than only results or talent. The child learns that worth does not depend on winning, and can risk trying hard things.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager boasts, mocks others or refuses to try to avoid being seen failing. Loud confidence often covers a fear of being exposed, and safe chances to fail help more than lectures.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager measures looks, followers and life against curated images and feels behind. Self-worth rises and falls with likes, and offline achievements and friendships give firmer ground.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A friend hears constant put-downs like I am so stupid and sees them decline chances. Shares honest, specific praise and stays close, and encourages talking to a trusted adult if the low mood persists.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A young adult asks for opinions before every decision and feels crushed by mild criticism. Approval works like a drug that fades quickly, and slowly building an inner sense of worth is the work.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26
